correctness.rationale: PASS. Apply intrinsic spherical coarea to the pair bisector F(z)=z·(Xi-Xj): on the zero set the gradient norm equals the generating-site chord. Fixing z by rotational invariance, the pair heights are iid uniform on [-1,1]; their equal-height coarea density is multiplied by the empty-cap probability ((1+c)/2)^(n-2), and the relative azimuth is uniform. The resulting unnormalized pair-arclength density sqrt(1-c²)sin(Delta/2)((1+c)/2)^(n-2) dc dDelta integrates to 16B(n-1/2,3/2), giving the stated finite-n total-length law after multiplying by binom(n,2). Transformation U=(1+c)/2 produces Beta(n-1/2,3/2); Z=cos(Delta/2) is uniform [-1,1], independent, giving V=1-Z²~Beta(1,1/2), Q=16U(1-U)V. Beta moment algebra yields all stated Q moments and, from n(1-U) -> Gamma(3/2,1), nQ/16 -> Exp(1). Boundary n=2 is a single full great-circle interface; triple ties have zero arclength. Independent exact rational beta-moment and small-n checks and source independent spherical polygon clipping corroborated the proof. This is annealed expected-arclength sampling, not a per-realization quenched law.
